title: Local formula and uniqueness for a first order formal adjoint
statement: Use the fields $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $U\subset\mathbf R^m$ be open, $m,r,s\geq1$, and let $H_E:U\to\operatorname{Mat}_{r\times r}(\mathbf C)$ and $H_F:U\to\operatorname{Mat}_{s\times s}(\mathbf C)$ be smooth positive definite Hermitian matrix functions, giving fibre inner products $\langle u,v\rangle_E=u^\dagger H_Ev$ and $\langle w,v\rangle_F=w^\dagger H_Fv$ (conjugate-linear in the first argument). Let $\rho:U\to\mathbf R_{>0}$ be a smooth positive density, let $A_j,B:U\to\operatorname{Mat}_{s\times r}(\mathbf C)$ be smooth, and set $Du=\sum_{j=1}^m A_j\partial_{t_j}u+Bu$. The unique complex-linear differential operator $D^*$ with smooth coefficients satisfying $$\int_U\langle Du,v\rangle_F\rho\,dt=\int_U\langle u,D^*v\rangle_E\rho\,dt$$ for all compactly supported smooth $u,v$ is of order at most one and is given, for every smooth $v$, by $$D^*v=H_E^{-1}\left(-\rho^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m\partial_{t_j}(\rho A_j^\dagger H_Fv)+B^\dagger H_Fv\right).$$ The dagger denotes conjugate transpose. These local expressions agree under smooth changes of real coordinates and complex bundle frames. Consequently the formula defines the unique formal adjoint of a smooth complex-linear first order differential operator between finite rank Hermitian vector bundles on any smooth manifold without boundary, with any smooth positive density; its restriction to a coordinate chart is the displayed formula. Compactness and completeness are not required. Zero rank source or target bundles give zero operators.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-coordinate-weighted-adjoint] with $L=D$ and the given matrices and density. Its operator $Q$ is smooth, complex-linear, and of order at most one, and satisfies the required integral identity, even when only one test section has compact support. Since $(\rho H_E)^{-1}=\rho^{-1}H_E^{-1}$ and real scalar multiplication commutes with every matrix, its displayed expression is exactly the asserted $D^*$. Thus the formula gives existence on every coordinate domain; no assumption on its boundary or on its compactness was used.

proof.text: First prove uniqueness on compactly supported inputs, on any open coordinate domain $W$. Suppose $P$ and $Q$ are two smooth differential operators satisfying the adjunction there, and fix $v\in C_c^\infty(W,\mathbf C^s)$. Set $w=(P-Q)v$. Subtracting the two adjunction identities gives $\int_W u^\dagger H_Ew\rho\,dt=0$ for every $u\in C_c^\infty(W,\mathbf C^r)$. For each standard basis vector $e_a$ choose $u=ge_a$, where $g$ is any smooth real scalar test with compact topological support in $W$. The continuous function $f_a=\rho(H_Ew)_a$, extended by zero outside $W$, is locally integrable on $W$ by [lem-sfb-continuous-local-integrability]. The preceding identity is exactly $\int_{\mathbf R^m}g f_a=0$, since $g$ vanishes outside $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-test-ae-separation] to obtain $f_a=0$ almost everywhere on $W$, and [lem-sfb-continuous-ae-pointwise] to upgrade to every point. The zero extension need only be continuous on $W$, which it is. Because $\rho>0$ and $H_E$ is invertible, all coordinates vanishing imply $w=0$. This works for every compactly supported $v$.

proof.text: To extend this uniqueness to every smooth local input $v$, fix $x\in W$ and radii $0<a<b$ with $\overline B(x,b)\subset W$. By [lem-sfb-euclidean-smooth-bump] choose $\beta=1$ on $\overline B(x,a)$ with compact support $\overline B(x,b)$. The section $\beta v$ on $W$, extended by zero, is smooth and compactly supported: near any point outside that closed ball it is identically zero. The preceding step gives $P(\beta v)=Q(\beta v)$. Since a differential operator depends only on the germ of its input and $\beta v=v$ near $x$, this equality at $x$ gives $Pv(x)=Qv(x)$. This argument allows $P$ to have any finite order. Consequently uniqueness holds among all the differential operators in the statement, not just among first order candidates.

proof.text: Compare two coordinate and frame descriptions on an overlap, writing $y=\phi(x)$, $u_x=P(x)u_y(\phi(x))$, and $v_x=R(x)v_y(\phi(x))$ with invertible smooth frame matrices $P,R$. The definitions of the metrics and the density give $H_{E,y}(\phi(x))=P^\dagger H_{E,x}P$, $H_{F,y}(\phi(x))=R^\dagger H_{F,x}R$, and $\rho_y(\phi(x))|\det d\phi_x|=\rho_x(x)$. Thus $u_x^\dagger H_{E,x}z_x=u_y^\dagger H_{E,y}z_y$ when $z_x=Pz_y\circ\phi$, and likewise for $F$. By [lem-sfb-euclidean-jacobian-integral] the corresponding scalar integrals are equal in the two charts, including orientation-reversing transitions. The smooth transition is a diffeomorphism between the open overlap domains, precisely the hypothesis of that node; compact test supports remain compact under it. Transfer the $x$-chart operator $Q_x$ by $\widetilde Q_y v_y=(P^{-1}Q_x(Rv_y\circ\phi))\circ\phi^{-1}$. The chain and product rules show directly that it is a smooth complex-linear differential operator of order at most one. The integral equalities just proved and the local adjunction of step 1 show that $\widetilde Q_y$ is adjoint to $D_yu_y=(R^{-1}D_x(Pu_y\circ\phi))\circ\phi^{-1}$. Steps 2 and 3, applied to this overlap, imply $\widetilde Q_y=Q_y$. This is the asserted compatibility.

proof.text: The compatible local outputs in step 4 define $D^*v$ for a smooth section $v$ of $F$: use $Q_xv_x$ in each trivializing coordinate chart. On overlaps those expressions represent the same vector of $E$, so the glued section is smooth and unique point by point. Locally it has the formula of step 1, hence defines a smooth complex-linear differential operator of order at most one. It remains to verify the global integral identity, since two compactly supported sections need not be supported in one chart.

proof.text: Let $u,v$ be compactly supported smooth sections on $M$ and put $K=\operatorname{supp}u$. Cover $K$ by finitely many trivializing coordinate domains $V_i$ and put $N=\bigcup_i V_i$. This open submanifold is Hausdorff and sigma-compact: each coordinate image is an open Euclidean set, covered by the countable family of closed rational balls contained in it, and finite unions preserve sigma-compactness. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subordinate-partition] on $N$ with the closed set $S=K$ and the finite open cover $(V_i)$. It gives smooth $\varphi_i$ with $\sum_i\varphi_i=1$ on $K$ and closed supports contained in $V_i$. Put $u_i=\varphi_i u$ on $N$ and extend by zero to $M$. Its support is a closed subset of $K$ contained in $V_i$, hence compact, and the zero extension is smooth since that support is contained in the open domain. Now $\sum_i u_i=u$ everywhere. Apply [lem-sfb-coordinate-weighted-adjoint] on $V_i$ to $u_i$ and the unrestricted smooth section $v|_{V_i}$; the cited statement allows only the first input to be compactly supported. Change-of-variables compatibility from step 4 identifies these integrals with the intrinsic density integrals. Sum the finitely many identities to obtain $\int_M\langle Du,v\rangle_F=\sum_i\int_M\langle Du_i,v\rangle_F=\sum_i\int_M\langle u_i,D^*v\rangle_E=\int_M\langle u,D^*v\rangle_E$. Linearity also gives $\sum_iDu_i=Du$, so no individual derivative of a partition function was discarded.

proof.text: If another global smooth differential operator satisfies the same identity, take both tests compactly supported inside a trivializing chart and extend them by zero. The identity restricts to that chart; steps 2 and 3 give equality on every smooth local input, and hence equality of the global operators. No completeness, total volume, or compactness of $M$ entered the construction: step 6 used only a neighborhood of the compact test support. If a bundle has rank zero, its sections are zero and both operators are zero; the assertion is interpreted without forming nonempty Gram matrices. In dimension zero the derivative sum is empty and pointwise finite-dimensional adjunction gives $D^*=H_E^{-1}B^\dagger H_F$; compact tests at a single point verify it and give uniqueness. On an empty chart all assertions are vacuous. These cases also glue pointwise.
